title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

baseProblem.statement: Given a sorted array that has been rotated at some unknown pivot (no duplicates), find the minimum element in O(log n) time.

options.conceptLabel: A pointer and a running min
options.rationale: Scanning with a running min is the O(n) approach; binary search needs converging bounds, not a linear accumulator.

options.conceptLabel: Low and high bounds over the array
options.rationale: The minimum sits at the rotation point; converging [lo, hi] bounds find it in O(log n).

options.conceptLabel: Only the high bound
options.rationale: You need both bounds to halve the range; one bound can't express which side to keep.

options.conceptLabel: A sorted copy of the array
options.rationale: Sorting is O(n log n) and trivially makes the first element the answer — but it defeats the O(log n) requirement.

options.conceptLabel: While lo is strictly less than hi
options.rationale: Converge until a single element remains; that survivor is the minimum.

options.conceptLabel: While lo is less than or equal to hi
options.rationale: With hi = mid (not mid - 1) this never terminates — lo and hi can stick and loop forever.

options.conceptLabel: Once per index
options.rationale: A linear pass is O(n), abandoning the log-time goal.

options.conceptLabel: While the ends are out of order
options.rationale: On a non-rotated or already-converged range this never enters, returning a wrong early answer.

rounds.question: What do you compute each step?

options.conceptLabel: The midpoint of the end values
options.rationale: mid must be an INDEX; averaging values and then indexing is meaningless.

options.conceptLabel: The midpoint index
options.rationale: Halving the index range is the core of binary search.

options.conceptLabel: The midpoint, rounded up
options.rationale: The upper mid combined with the 'hi = mid' branch can stall progress; the lower mid pairs correctly with this comparison.

options.conceptLabel: A random index in range

fragments.java: int mid = lo + new Random().nextInt(hi - lo + 1);

options.rationale: A random probe destroys both the O(log n) guarantee and determinism.

rounds.question: How do you pick the half containing the minimum?

options.conceptLabel: If mid exceeds the high value go right, else keep mid

fragments.java: if (nums[mid] > nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;

options.rationale: nums[mid] > nums[hi] means the rotation (and the min) is to mid's right; otherwise the min is at mid or left, so keep mid.

options.conceptLabel: Compare mid to the low value instead

fragments.java: if (nums[mid] > nums[lo]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;

options.rationale: Comparing to nums[lo] misclassifies an already-sorted left side, sending you away from the minimum.

options.conceptLabel: Always halve to the left
options.rationale: Ignoring the comparison drives hi down even when the min is to the right, returning the wrong element.

options.conceptLabel: Exclude mid on the keep-left branch too

fragments.java: if (nums[mid] > nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;

options.rationale: hi = mid - 1 can skip over the minimum itself when mid is the min; you must keep mid as a candidate.

options.conceptLabel: The element at lo
options.rationale: The loop converges lo and hi onto the rotation point, where the minimum lives.

options.conceptLabel: lo, the index
options.rationale: The problem asks for the minimum VALUE, not its index.

options.conceptLabel: The first element
options.rationale: Only correct for an unrotated array; after rotation the first element isn't the min.

options.conceptLabel: The element at mid
options.rationale: mid is the last probe, not necessarily the converged minimum position.
